Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Money, work & business · Household, washing & chores

safe noun

a strongbox for money

also strongbox, money box, cash box, coffer, safe-deposit box

classical

Hor. S. 1.1.67: nummōs contemplor in arcā (Lewis & Short)
Juv. 1.89–90

arca, arcae f.

noun, first declension

a strongbox, a safe; a chest

A chest or box of any kind (see chest), and above all the strongbox where money was kept; so, by metonymy, one’s money: arcae nostrae cōnfīditō, count on my purse (Cic. Att. 1.9).

Other words

  • armārium, armāriī n. — a cupboard, a closet; one that holds money

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Clu. 64 (Lewis & Short); Plaut. Capt. 4.4.10

    A cupboard or closet for food, clothes or money: Cicero speaks of one in a house that held “a fair sum of money and gold” (Clu. 64). Its everyday sense is a cupboard (see cupboard).

  • dēpositōrium, dēpositōriī n. — a safe-deposit box

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · Traupman 373

    Traupman’s word, for a box rented in a bank.

Examples

  • populus mē sībilat, at mihi plaudō ipse domī, simul ac nummōs contemplor in arcā

    the people hiss me, but I applaud myself at home as soon as I gaze at the money in my strongboxHor. S. 1.1.66–67

See also chest, till, money, bank, safe.

SourcesLewis & Short: arca · Lewis & Short: armarium
